title: Karl Organizing: Mutual aid disaster relief
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mutual aid disaster relief] How do we organize disaster relief?

Real talk: Move fast and skip the bureaucracy. Set up a supply hub in an accessible location. Use social media and group chats to coordinate needs and offers. Prioritize the most vulnerable: elderly, disabled, undocumented neighbors who can't access official aid. Document what you distribute. Mutual aid fills the gaps the state leaves — and the state always leaves gaps.

title: Karl Organizing: Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Messaging] How do we make sure people know why we're actually out here?

Keep your demands punchy and your banners even punchier. Pick one clear target—like a specific landlord or a union-busting CEO—and blast their name across every sign so the message cannot be twisted by corporate media. If a passerby asks what is up, have a ten-second pitch ready that connects our struggle directly to the empty wallet in their pocket.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: social Media OPSEC] Give me the short version: Should I make my accounts private?

Here's the thing: Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining the Work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining the Work] I'm exhausted and feel like I'm burning out. How do I keep going?

Take a damn break and let the rest of the collective carry the load for a while. Mutual aid isn't a solo performance; it's a relay race where we pass the baton when our legs get heavy. If you burn yourself out, you're no good to the movement or your neighbors, so go rest and recharge. We're in this for the long haul, and that means pacing ourselves so we can see the revolution through to the end.

title: Karl Organizing: Protest safety kit
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Protest safety kit] What should I bring to a protest?

Water, snacks, a mask, ID, cash, a charged phone, and a buddy you never separate from. Write the legal hotline number on your arm in Sharpie. Don't bring anything you can't afford to lose. Dress for weather and for running. And leave the face-unlock on — set a passcode, since cops can compel your face but not your code in most places.

title: Karl Organizing: The 80/20 rule
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 80/20 rule] I feel like I'm doing all the talking in these meetings. Is that bad?

You're failing if you're the one talking. You should be listening 80% of the time and talking 20%. Your job is to uncover their 'issues'—the things that make them angry enough to fight. People don't join unions because of your speech; they join because they want to fix their own lives. Ask open-ended questions and let their own grievances drive them to action. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accountability] Can you explain: what if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way.

title: Karl Organizing: Aggressive Bystanders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Aggressive Bystanders] What if a driver tries to push through our line?

Safety is the priority, so have your marshals use bikes or heavy banners to create a buffer between the cars and the crowd. Never engage in a shouting match with a driver; just keep the march moving and use your collective mass to maintain the space. If a vehicle gets truly dangerous, the marshals should signal the crowd to move to the sidewalk immediately to avoid a tragedy.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: encrypted Messaging] Give me the short version: What are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?

Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: power Mapping] Give me the short version: How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?

Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] A friend asked me: 'How do we handle money and tools between different groups?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else.

title: Karl Organizing: Tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tactical Diversity] A friend asked me: 'Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?' What do I tell them?

Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Press Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Press Strategy] How should we handle reporters who show up at the action?

Designate two or three press flacks who know the talking points inside and out, and tell everyone else to point microphones toward them. Don't let reporters bait you into 'both sides' nonsense; stick to the facts of how the billionaires are bleeding us dry. Never give your full legal name to a reporter unless you have cleared it with the organizers and the legal team first. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food Sourcing] A friend asked me: 'We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?' What do I tell them?

Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: post-Election Discipline
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: post-Election Discipline] Give me the short version: What do we do the day after we win?

We go right back to the doors. Thank the voters, but tell them the real work starts now and you need them to keep the pressure on. Set up a regular 'People's Assembly' in your district to keep yourself accountable and to give the community a direct line to your office. Winning the seat is just opening the door; the movement is what walks through it to actually change the world.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, avoiding Sectarianism
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, avoiding Sectarianism] There is a group we have beef with, but they agree with us on this campaign. Do we work with them?

I don't care if you hate their stickers or their favorite dead theorist. If they are willing to put boots on the pavement to stop an eviction or challenge a billionaire, they are a temporary comrade. Keep the internal beef for the pub and keep your eyes on the ruling class's throat; we don't have the luxury of purity tests when the rent is due. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Food Distribution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food Distribution] How do we get groceries to people who need them without looking like a charity?

Karl's answer: Set up a grocery hub where people can help pack bags and decide what's on the menu together. Focus on building relationships with the people coming by rather than just handing out boxes and checking names. It's about breaking bread and building power, not making yourself feel like a hero. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: ICE watch
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[ICE watch] What do I do if I see ICE in my neighborhood?

Let me break it down: Verify first — don't spread panic over a rumor. If confirmed, alert the rapid response network immediately. Film from a distance. Remind neighbors of their rights: don't open the door, don't sign anything, ask for a judicial warrant. Connect families with immigration lawyers. Speed and calm save people.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Hygiene] Give me the short version: Is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?

Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack.

title: Karl Organizing: Time Bank Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Time Bank Value] In a time bank, is an hour of plumbing worth more than an hour of childcare?

Let me break it down: Absolutely not. In our world, an hour of a human being's life is equal regardless of the task they're performing. The capitalists want us to believe some labor is 'unskilled' so they can pay us pennies, but we know better. Whether you're fixing a pipe or watching a comrade's kid so they can organize, you're contributing to our collective survival. We value the person, not the market price of their sweat.

title: Karl Organizing: Signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signature Gathering] Can you explain: how do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

Here's the thing: You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: Rent strike risks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rent strike risks] Is a rent strike legal? What are the risks?

It depends on your state — some protect it, some don't. The real question is whether you have the numbers: a rent strike with 10% participation gets you evicted; with 70% it gets you a meeting. Put rent in escrow to show good faith. Get a tenant lawyer BEFORE you start, not after. And document everything the landlord does — retaliation is illegal almost everywhere, but only if you can prove it.

title: Karl Organizing: Transit Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transit Policy] What's the radical approach to local transit?

Make it free and make it frequent. Public transit should be a service like the library or the fire department, funded by taxing the corporations that benefit from workers being able to get to their jobs. Fight for dedicated bus lanes and expanded routes that serve the neighborhoods the current system ignores. Mobility is a right, and we should be taking the streets back from private cars and giving them to the people. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] What do I do if some guy starts screaming in my face while we're marching?

Keep your cool and do not let their bait pull you into a cage. Use your body to create a physical barrier between the agitator and the rest of the march, and move the targeted comrade to the center of the group. If you engage, keep your voice low and steady, because their goal is to cause a scene that justifies a police crackdown while the ruling class watches and laughs. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, metadata Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, metadata Awareness] What is 'scrubbing' and how do I do it?

Scrubbing means stripping the hidden data—location, camera type, time—from your files. Use an app like 'ImagePipe' on Android or 'Metapho' on iOS before sharing any protest photos. For PDFs and docs, use the 'ExifTool' or simple online scrubbers. This prevents the state from using a 'cool photo' to pinpoint exactly where you stood at 2:00 PM.

title: Karl Organizing: Merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Merch Strategy] A friend asked me: 'What kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action.

title: Karl Organizing: Labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Labor Endorsements] A friend asked me: 'How do I get unions to back a radical campaign?' What do I tell them?

Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office.

title: Karl Organizing: Local Press
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Local Press] The local paper is biased against me. How do I get my message out?

Stop begging them for coverage and start making your own media. Record your own videos, write your own newsletters, and use your volunteers to spread the word through every apartment building in the district. When the press does show up, be polite but firm, and always bring the conversation back to your platform. If they won't tell the truth about the struggle, we'll shout it from every porch until they can't ignore us.

title: Karl Organizing: Ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ethical Banking] Can you explain: where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Tool Libraries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tool Libraries] How do we stop people from stealing or breaking the tools in our sharing library?

Trust is our currency, but a simple checkout sheet and a 'how-to' guide for expensive gear keeps things running smooth. If someone breaks a drill, they don't get punished; we just ask them to help the crew learn how to fix it. People take care of things when they realize the tool belongs to the whole community, not some faceless corporation. Keep a small fund for repairs by asking comrades to chip in a few bucks when they can. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Internal Conflict
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Internal Conflict] What do we do when two groups in the coalition start fighting each other?

Real talk: Drag them back to the shared demand and remind them who the real enemy is. If the beef is personal, tell them to settle it on their own time because the warehouse workers or the tenants are waiting on us to lead. We aren't here to be a family; we are here to be a fist, and a fist doesn't work if the fingers are trying to snap each other.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, surveillance Awareness] How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Flyering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Flyering] How do I make a flyer that people won't just throw away?

Real talk: Karl's answer: Put the biggest problem your neighbors face in huge letters at the top and keep the text short. Use high-contrast colors and a clear call to action, like a meeting date or a phone number to call. Hand them to people directly with a quick word instead of just tucking them under windshield wipers.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Counter-Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Counter-Fundraising] Can you explain: how do we use our opposition to raise money?

Nothing opens wallets faster than a common enemy. When a billionaire or a corrupt politician attacks your movement, use their own words to show your supporters why we're winning. Frame every contribution as a direct middle finger to the people trying to silence us, and watch the resources pour in from people who are fed up.

title: Karl Organizing: Election day
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Election day] What should we do on the day of the NLRB election?

Treat it like a celebration of your power. Have people wear their union colors and make sure every single 'yes' vote gets to the polls. Use your map to track who has voted and who needs a nudge. The boss will be watching, so stay disciplined and joyful. You've done the work, you've built the supermajority, now go in there and take what's yours.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: inclusivity in Action] Give me the short version: How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] Can you explain: is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?

It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Rent strike risks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rent strike risks] Is a rent strike legal? What are the risks?

It depends on your state — some protect it, some don't. The real question is whether you have the numbers: a rent strike with 10% participation gets you evicted; with 70% it gets you a meeting. Put rent in escrow to show good faith. Get a tenant lawyer BEFORE you start, not after. And document everything the landlord does — retaliation is illegal almost everywhere, but only if you can prove it. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: long-term Planning] Give me the short version: How do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Real talk: Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, benefit Events
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, benefit Events] We want to host a fundraiser but don't have a budget for a venue. What do we do?

Find a comrade with a backyard or a local dive bar that hates the status quo as much as we do. Throw a rent party with local bands or a radical trivia night where the entry fee goes straight into the war chest. You don't need a ballroom when you have a community willing to pack into a basement for the cause.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: the Ask
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: the Ask] Give me the short version: What's the best way to phrase a request for funds on social media?

Here's how it works: Be direct, be urgent, and skip the flowery language. Tell them exactly what the crisis is, what we're doing to stop it, and exactly how much we need to get the job done. People want to be part of a winning fight, so show them that their five dollars is the literal fuel for the next victory.

title: Karl Organizing: Mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mapping Vulnerability] A friend asked me: 'How do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?' What do I tell them?

Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: harm Reduction
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: harm Reduction] Give me the short version: People are using drugs near our community fridge. How do we handle this safely?

Stop judging and start helping; hand out clean needles and Narcan instead of calling the cops who will only make it worse. Train your fridge volunteers on how to spot an overdose and how to use a reversal kit without hesitating. We treat our neighbors with dignity, especially those the system has discarded and left to struggle with addiction. Safety comes from community care and presence, not from displacement and state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action] The landlord is ignoring our letters. What's the next step?

If they won't hear you, make it so they can't ignore you. Take the union to the landlord's office, their church, or their favorite restaurant and pass out flyers to everyone they know. Disrupt their 'good reputation' in the community. When you make their private greed a public embarrassment, the cost of fixing your plumbing suddenly becomes cheaper than the cost of the bad publicity.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, bail Prep
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, bail Prep] How do I handle bail if I don't have much money?

Real talk: Before the action, identify a local community bail fund or pool resources with your affinity group to create an emergency pot. We look out for our own, and we don't let billionaires' prices keep our comrades in cages. If you're inside, wait for the word from legal support; we are coming to get you out.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: First Meeting Agenda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[First Meeting Agenda] We're having our first building-wide meeting. What should we talk about?

Keep it short and focused on action, not just complaining. Start by listing the top three problems everyone shares, like heat or pests, and then pick one concrete goal to achieve by next month. Assign tasks: someone handles the contact list, someone drafts the demand letter, and someone else researches the landlord's assets. Leave that room with a plan, not just a list of grievances. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, mapping Vulnerability

Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be.

title: Karl Organizing: Signing union cards
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signing union cards] When is the right time to start collecting signed union cards?

You don't pull out the cards until you've already had deep 1-on-1 conversations with at least half the shop. A card isn't just a piece of paper; it’s a commitment to fight. If you start passing them out too early, you'll tip off the boss before you're ready. Wait until the energy is high and your leaders are ready to move fast to get a supermajority.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: free Clinic Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: free Clinic Logistics] Give me the short version: I want to start a free clinic, but none of us are doctors. Is it still possible?

You don't need a medical degree to run a first-aid station or a herbal medicine collective, so start where you are. Focus on preventative care, wound cleaning, and distributing naloxone to keep our people alive in the streets. Partner with sympathetic nurses or EMTs who are tired of the insurance industry's greed and want to actually help folks. We're building a parallel system of care because the private hospitals would rather see us die than see us broke.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining Momentum
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining Momentum] How do we keep people from burning out during a long campaign?

Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing everything, and make sure you're celebrating the small wins along the way. Organize social events that aren't just about strategy—have a meal, play music, and remind yourselves why you're fighting for a better world in the first place. You can't win a marathon if you're sprinting until your lungs give out in the first week.

title: Karl Organizing: Donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Donor Capture] A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement.

title: Karl Organizing: The First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The First Meeting] A friend asked me: 'What is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?' What do I tell them?

Look, Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Sectarianism
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Campaign Literature
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Campaign Literature] A friend asked me: 'What should my flyers look like?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Bold, clear, and high-contrast. No small print and no flowery language. Put your face on there so people know you're a neighbor, and list three concrete things you will do on Day One to make their lives easier. Use union printers and include the bug to show you support organized labor. Every flyer should have a clear call to action: join the fight, chip in to pool resources, or show up at the polls.

Real talk: Scrubbing means stripping the hidden data—location, camera type, time—from your files. Use an app like 'ImagePipe' on Android or 'Metapho' on iOS before sharing any protest photos. For PDFs and docs, use the 'ExifTool' or simple online scrubbers. This prevents the state from using a 'cool photo' to pinpoint exactly where you stood at 2:00 PM.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: political Education
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: political Education] Give me the short version: Should we charge for our reading groups and pamphlets?

Look, Cover your costs, but never turn a profit on knowledge. Charge enough for the physical books or zines to fund the next print run, and always have a 'pay what you can' stack for comrades who are broke. Our goal is to arm the working class with ideas, not to gatekeep the revolution behind a paywall.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, skill-sharing for Cash] How can we raise money using our own talents?

Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Propaganda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Propaganda] A friend asked me: 'The local news is lying about our coalition. How do we fight back?' What do I tell them?

Stop begging the corporate media for scraps of coverage and become your own media outlet. Use your combined social media reach, print your own newsletters, and talk directly to your neighbors on their doorsteps. When the billionaires own the newspapers, the only truth people will hear is the truth you tell them face-to-face and the results they see with their own eyes. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: identifying Undercovers] Give me the short version: How can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?

Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Election Discipline
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Election Discipline] Can you explain: what do we do the day after we win?

We go right back to the doors. Thank the voters, but tell them the real work starts now and you need them to keep the pressure on. Set up a regular 'People's Assembly' in your district to keep yourself accountable and to give the community a direct line to your office. Winning the seat is just opening the door; the movement is what walks through it to actually change the world.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action Support] Can you explain: how do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.
